# everpure_azure_volumes (Data Source)

Lists the Volumes in a Volume Group. Soft-deleted (destroyed, not yet eradicated) volumes are excluded by default; set `include_destroyed = true` to include them.

To look up a single, already-known volume, use the [`everpure_azure_volume` data source](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/data-sources/volume) instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

data "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  name            = "vg-prod-east"
  storage_pool_id = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east"
}

# Lists every volume in the volume group above, including soft-deleted
# (destroyed, not yet eradicated) ones.
data "everpure_azure_volumes" "example" {
  volume_group_id   = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  include_destroyed = true
}

# Volume IDs keyed by name.
output "volume_ids_by_name" {
  value = {
    for v in data.everpure_azure_volumes.example.volumes :
    v.name => v.id
  }
}

locals {
  # Every soft-deleted volume that was named "vol-prod-data", oldest first.
  deleted_vol_prod_data = [
    for v in data.everpure_azure_volumes.example.volumes :
    v if v.soft_deletion != null && v.soft_deletion.previous_name == "vol-prod-data"
  ]
  newest_deleted_vol_prod_data_id = (
    length(local.deleted_vol_prod_data) > 0
    ? local.deleted_vol_prod_data[length(local.deleted_vol_prod_data) - 1].id
    : null
  )
}

# Recovers the most recently soft-deleted "vol-prod-data", if there is one.
resource "everpure_azure_volume" "recovered" {
  count                        = local.newest_deleted_vol_prod_data_id == null ? 0 : 1
  name                         = "vol-prod-data-recovered"
  volume_group_id              = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  source_type                  = "recoverableVolume"
  source_recoverable_volume_id = local.newest_deleted_vol_prod_data_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group to list volumes in. Must be in the provider's own `subscription_id`.

### Optional

- `include_destroyed` (Boolean) Whether to include soft-deleted (destroyed, not yet eradicated) volumes in the result. Defaults to `false`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `volumes` (Attributes List) The volumes found, sorted by `id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volumes))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the volumes.


<a id="nestedatt--volumes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volumes`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume.
- `name` (String) Name of the volume. A soft-deleted volume's name is the timestamped name it was renamed to on deletion; see `soft_deletion.previous_name` for its original name.
- `provisioned_size_in_bytes` (Number) Provisioned size of the volume, in bytes.
- `serial_number` (String) The volume's own serial number. Visible in the VM as the disk/drive serial number.
- `soft_deletion` (Attributes) Soft-delete state, present only when this volume is soft-deleted (destroyed, not yet eradicated). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volumes--soft_deletion))
- `space` (Attributes) Space usage, in bytes. Null when the service reports none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volumes--space))
- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group this volume lives on. Same as the data source's own `volume_group_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--volumes--soft_deletion"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volumes.soft_deletion`

Read-Only:

- `destroyed_at` (String) When it was destroyed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `eradication_timestamp` (String) Approximate time at which the object will be eradicated automatically, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Derived from the remaining retention when read, so it can change by seconds to minutes between reads; do not use it for exact comparisons or as an input to other resources. Use `destroyed_at` as the stable reference.
- `previous_name` (String) The name this volume had before it was destroyed.


<a id="nestedatt--volumes--space"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volumes.space`

Read-Only:

- `shared_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by duplicated data, meaning data shared among different volumes and snapshots as a result of data deduplication, in bytes.
- `snapshots_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by data unique to one or more snapshots, in bytes.
- `total_used_in_bytes` (Number) Total space occupied by customer data, in bytes. This is the space being billed for.
- `unique_in_bytes` (Number) Unique space occupied by customer data, in bytes.
